headline: Breathwork, from entry to detail
overview:
The Breathwork tool is your personal breathing coach, offering guided breathing exercises right in your browser. It features a beautiful animated visual guide that expands and contracts to help you match your breath to the rhythm. Whether you're looking to calm anxiety, improve focus, or just take a mindful pause in your day, there's a breathing pattern here for you.

The tool comes with 8 breathwork patterns (like Box Breathing, 4-7-8, and Alternate Nostril) plus 8 nervous system exercises (like Horse Stance and Cat-Cow Breathing). Each session can be timed from 1 to 8 minutes, and your practice history is tracked so you can build a consistent habit.
targetAudience: Anyone looking to reduce stress, improve focus, or build a daily mindfulness practice. No experience needed — the visual guide and step-by-step instructions make it easy to follow along, even if you've never tried breathwork before.

steps.title: Landing Page — Choose Your Practice
steps.description:
When you open the Breathwork tool, you'll see the main breathing interface. At the center is a large animated circle with the current breathing pattern name (defaulting to Box Breathing). Below it, you can select your session duration — 2, 4, 6, or 8 minutes. The "Start Practice" button kicks off your session.

At the bottom, you'll find quick links to your History, Progress stats, a Learn section with breathing science, and custom Sequences you can create.
steps.screenshotAlt: Breathwork landing page showing the breathing circle, duration selector, and Start Practice button

steps.title: Choose a Breathing Pattern
steps.description:
Tap "Change" to open the pattern selector. You'll see two categories:

• Breathwork — 8 classic breathing techniques including Simple Breath Awareness, Box Breathing, 4-7-8 Breathing, Diaphragmatic Breathing, Resonant Breathing, Alternate Nostril, Pursed-Lip, and Humming Bee Breath (Brahmari). Each shows the estimated session time.

• Nervous System — 8 body-based exercises like Horse Stance, Standing Meditation (Zhan Zhuang), Cat-Cow Breathing, and Warrior Breath. These include posture descriptions to help you get into the right position.

The currently selected pattern is highlighted with a checkmark.

steps.title: Read the Instructions
steps.description:
Before starting, you can tap "Instructions" to see step-by-step guidance for your chosen breathing pattern. For Box Breathing, the instructions walk you through the posture (sit upright, feet flat), preparation (close eyes, exhale fully), and the four-phase cycle: inhale for 4 counts, hold for 4, exhale for 4, hold empty for 4.

This is especially helpful when trying a new pattern for the first time.

steps.title: Active Breathing Session
steps.description:
Once you hit "Start Practice," the screen transforms into an immersive, full-screen breathing guide. The background goes dark to minimize distractions, and a large animated shape (matching the breathing pattern — a square for Box Breathing) pulses to guide your breath.

The current phase is displayed in the center (Inhale, Hold, Exhale, or Hold) with a countdown number. A timer at the bottom shows remaining session time. You can Pause or Reset at any time, and there are buttons in the bottom-right to change the visual theme or toggle ambient sound.

Press ESC or the X button to end the session early.

keyFeatures: 16 breathing patterns across Breathwork and Nervous System categories
Immersive full-screen guided sessions with animated visual cues
Step-by-step instructions for each breathing technique
Theme and ambient sound customization during sessions
Practice history tracking and progress statistics
Custom breathing sequences you can create and save
Learn section with the science behind each technique
tips: Start with Box Breathing or Simple Breath Awareness if you're new to breathwork
Use the 2-minute sessions to build a daily habit before increasing duration
Try the Nervous System exercises if you want something more physical
Check your Progress page weekly to see your consistency streak
The 4-7-8 technique is particularly good right before sleep
